title: UrbanExpert: Task-Conditioned Multi-Modal Fusion via Semantic Expert Routing for Urban Socioeconomic Prediction

problem.claim: Urban indicator prediction requires fusing heterogeneous modalities, but task-relevant feature combinations differ and related tasks may share cues.

gap.claim: Existing task-specific and task-agnostic approaches fail to share task knowledge appropriately, ignore inter-task semantic correlations, and assume complete modality observations.

contributions.claim: UrbanExpert conditions multi-modal fusion on task semantics while accommodating incomplete modality observations.
The framework recovers missing modality representations through cross-modal reconstruction and routes tasks to relevant experts using semantic affinity with learnable expert prototypes.
The model jointly optimizes prediction, reconstruction, and routing regularization objectives.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two real-world urban datasets reportedly show consistent improvement over single-task and multi-task baselines.
The authors report that the learned routing structure generalizes effectively to unseen tasks and cities.

narrative_sequence.summary: Urban indicator prediction must combine heterogeneous modalities whose usefulness varies by task.
Prior task-specific and task-agnostic paradigms do not adequately share semantic knowledge and generally assume complete observations.
UrbanExpert reconstructs missing modalities and uses task-semantic routing across experts to produce task-conditioned embeddings.
The authors report gains over single-task and multi-task baselines and generalization to unseen tasks and cities.

unknowns: Names and characteristics of the two urban datasets
